name: Minelauva
description: A star 61 parsecs away, 66 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: radius 65.88 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 697.427 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: effective temperature 3657 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.171)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 0.8 from 2012ApJ...761..161S, the median of its 2 spectra; the 8 published values span log g 0.8 to 1.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: distance 60.827 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 61 parsecs away, 66 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 697 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,657 K, so 65.88 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 63090: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Delta Virginis
quotes.card: Delta Virginis, formally named Minelauva, is a star in the zodiac constellation of Virgo.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 3.4, this star is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3704342295607157120 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
